source_text: Pharao praecipit populo infantem Hebraeum in flumen proici. Princeps mundi primordia nativitatis insidiatur. Christus post baptismum in desertum ductus tentatur — exemplar victoriae. Masculus generatus — opus Dei, eleemosyna — occultandus est; si coram hominibus iustitia, Aegyptii rapiunt et demergunt. Nolite fabulas veterum putare, sed ordinem vitae discite.
pass_a_gloss: Pharaoh commands to-people Hebrew infant into river to-be-thrown. Prince of-world beginnings of-birth lies-in-wait. Christ after baptism into desert led is-tempted — pattern of-victory. Male generated — work of-God, alms — to-be-hidden is; if before humans justice, Egyptians seize and sink. Do-not stories of-ancients think, but order of-life learn.
pass_b_english: Pharaoh next bids his people seize the Hebrew infant at birth and cast him into the river. So the [[prince of this world >> Bible:John 16:11]] ambushes our beginnings — as Jesus, [[led by the Spirit into the desert to be tempted >> Bible:Matthew 4:1]], opened the path of victory by fasting and prayer. If I give alms, I beget a “male,” a work of God; but if I do it [[to be seen by people >> Bible:Matthew 6:1]], Egyptians snatch it and drown it. Hide what the right hand does; [[pray to the Father in secret >> Bible:Matthew 6:6]]. You who hear are not being told old tales, but taught the order of a living faith.
